prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: stdio_server creates its read/write MemoryObjectStreams with buffer size 0 (unbuffered), so a sender's call to send() blocks until the receiver task is ready to receive. prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string input value whose field annotation is not exactly `str`. For union annotations like `str | None`, this corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. the literal strings "true", "123", "null", "[1,2]") by silently converting them to bool/int/None/list instead of leaving them as the intended string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string input value whose field annotation is not exactly `str`. For union annotations like `str | None`, this corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. the literal strings "true", "123", "null", "[1,2]") by silently converting them to bool/int/None/list instead of leaving them as the intended string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to skip pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` first strips `Annotated[...]` via `_unwrap_annotated` before checking the union members, so it correctly disables pre-parsing for `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` — the idiomatic way to write a described optional string parameter in mcpserver tools. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks raw union args against a fixed `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set without unwrapping `Annotated`, so an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` union member is never matched as simple and pre-parsing still fires, leaving the bug unfixed for that common case. #2032 does cover a couple of extra union shapes (e.g. `str | int`), but that added breadth doesn't offset missing the Annotated-wrapped case #3056 targets.

members.author: yaowubarbara

clusters.pick_reason: #2253 provides the end-to-end mechanism: it closes every tracked entry in self._sse_stream_writers inside terminate(), and updates streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown lifespan() to terminate active sessions before cancelling tasks, which is what actually stops the ASGI-incomplete-response errors on shutdown. #3218 only adds registration of the GET-stream writer into that same dict, and its own added comment ('Also expected when terminate()/close_sse_stream() closes the writer') shows it depends on the closing behavior #2253 supplies, making it a narrower, dependent slice of the same fix rather than a standalone one.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes the bug once at the MCPError base class via a module-level _restore_mcp_error(error_type, args) that does MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ and relies on the third __reduce__ tuple element to restore instance __dict__ (e.g. _elicitations) generically. This covers every subclass without enumerating constructor signatures. 2478's _restore_mcp_error instead special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError with an if/else calling from_error vs from_error_data, so any future subclass with a non-matching constructor needs a new branch. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, leaving the base MCPError.__reduce__ problem unaddressed for other subclasses. 3262's test diff also imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix was verified across multiple subclasses rather than just the one named in the issue.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key — this can falsely 409 an unrelated id, or still cross-wire responses between an int id and a string id with the same text, and it doesn't guard against a string id literally equal to `_GET_stream` colliding with GET_STREAM_KEY. #3221 introduces `_request_stream_key()` with explicit `i:`/`s:` prefixes, resolving both edge cases that #3063's simpler `str(id)` key leaves open, while fixing the same underlying duplicate-id race.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a helper to skip pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but #3056's `_is_optional_str` first strips `Annotated[...]` via `_unwrap_annotated` before checking the union members, so it correctly disables pre-parsing for `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` — the idiomatic way to write a described optional string parameter in mcpserver tools. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks raw union args against a fixed `_SIMPLE_TYPES` set without unwrapping `Annotated`, so an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` union member is never matched as simple and pre-parsing still fires, leaving the bug unfixed for that common case. #2032 does cover a couple of extra union shapes (e.g. `str | int`), but that added breadth doesn't offset missing the Annotated-wrapped case #3056 targets.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes the bug once at the MCPError base class via a module-level _restore_mcp_error(error_type, args) that does MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__ and relies on the third __reduce__ tuple element to restore instance __dict__ (e.g. _elicitations) generically. This covers every subclass without enumerating constructor signatures. 2478's _restore_mcp_error instead special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError with an if/else calling from_error vs from_error_data, so any future subclass with a non-matching constructor needs a new branch. 2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, leaving the base MCPError.__reduce__ problem unaddressed for other subclasses. 3262's test diff also imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix was verified across multiple subclasses rather than just the one named in the issue.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key — this can falsely 409 an unrelated id, or still cross-wire responses between an int id and a string id with the same text, and it doesn't guard against a string id literally equal to `_GET_stream` colliding with GET_STREAM_KEY. #3221 introduces `_request_stream_key()` with explicit `i:`/`s:` prefixes, resolving both edge cases that #3063's simpler `str(id)` key leaves open, while fixing the same underlying duplicate-id race.
